question.problem:
Solve the linear congruence $2x≡3\,(\text{mod}\,5)$ using trial and error. Express your answer as a nonnegative integer smaller than $5.$

$x≡$
{{field-1}}$\,(\text{mod}\,5)$
question.worked_solution:
Since the modulus $n=5$ is fairly small, we can solve the congruence by trial and error. 

Substituting $x=0,1,2,3,4$ into the congruence, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}2\cdot 0 & ≡0≢3 &  & (\text{mod}\,5) &  & \times  \\ 2\cdot 1 & ≡2≢3 &  & (\text{mod}\,5) &  & \times  \\ 2\cdot 2 & ≡4≢3 &  & (\text{mod}\,5) &  & \times  \\ 2\cdot 3 & ≡6≡5+1≡1≢3 &  & (\text{mod}\,5) &  & \times  \\ 2\cdot 4 & ≡8≡5+3≡3 &  & (\text{mod}\,5) &  & ✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x≡4\,(\text{mod}\,5).$

**Note**: Any number congruent to $4$ modulo $5$ is a solution. For example, note that $9≡4,$ and this also satisfies our congruence:

$$
\begin{aligned}2x & ≡2\cdot 9\, &  & (\text{mod}\,5) \\  & ≡18\, &  & (\text{mod}\,5) \\  & ≡3\cdot 5+3\, &  & (\text{mod}\,5) \\  & ≡0+3\, &  & (\text{mod}\,5) \\  & ≡3\,\,✓\, &  & (\text{mod}\,5)\end{aligned}
$$
